findings.title: .buffmap version field is written but never validated on deserialization
findings.description: MAP_FORMAT_VERSION (=1) is stamped into every .buffmap (L135) and the module doc (L17-22) claims consumers can use it to detect schema changes, but deserialize() (L93-96) parses BuffMapFile and calls from_buff_map_file() (L151) without ever comparing file.version to MAP_FORMAT_VERSION. The panic hook reads sidecars through this exact path (panic_hook.rs:60 read_from_file). A future v2 sidecar is silently accepted by a v1 reader and misparsed as garbage mappings instead of failing with a clear version error.
findings.root_cause: Version field added for forward-compat documentation, but no guard was implemented in the deserialization path when the format shipped (T24).
findings.impact: On any future schema bump, stale readers produce wrong panic-trace remaps or silently empty traces instead of an actionable 'unsupported .buffmap version' error; external consumers (DAP, backtrace tooling) inheriting deserialize() get the same silent misread.
findings.recommendation: In deserialize(), after parsing BuffMapFile, check file.version == MAP_FORMAT_VERSION and return a serde_json::Error when file.version > MAP_FORMAT_VERSION; accept older versions only while mappings remain compatible. Add a unit test with version: 2 asserting the error.
findings.fix_guide: 1. Add the version guard in format.rs::deserialize. 2. Add test: JSON with version 2 must error; version 1 must round-trip. 3. Run cargo test -p buff-lang-debug-info. 4. Keep ErrorCode-free (serde_json error is fine; no new E-code needed).

detection_method.query: grep MAP_FORMAT_VERSION|.version across crates -> only writer (L135) and test touch it; deserialize has no check

confidence.rationale: Directly verified: deserialize body contains no version comparison; panic hook confirmed to consume this path.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Code-level absence verified by reading the entire function and grepping all MAP_FORMAT_VERSION uses (none a read-side check). Doc comment explicitly promises detection capability that is not implemented.

findings.title: T57 registry endpoints return ad-hoc json! bodies duplicating typed DTO shapes
findings.description: multipart_publish (L831-838) hand-builds {name, version, deps} via serde_json::json!, byte-shaping the same object as the typed PublishResponse DTO (storage.rs:159-166) returned by the legacy POST /api/v1/publish (handlers.rs:468-473). get_stats (L897-900) emits {name, downloads} with no DTO struct at all, unlike every other endpoint (SearchResultRow, ResolveResponse, PackageMetadata). The registry has no published schema, so these untyped bodies are the de-facto contract.
findings.root_cause: T57 endpoints were added alongside (not on top of) the T126 typed-DTO layer; the json! shortcut was taken for a two-field echo and a two-field stats body.
findings.impact: If PublishResponse gains a field (e.g. published_at), the two publish endpoints' 201 bodies silently diverge and CLI/client parsers of one endpoint miss data the other returns; get_stats has zero compile-time protection against key renames breaking consumers.
findings.recommendation: Return Json(PublishResponse{..}) from multipart_publish (identical wire shape today, so non-breaking) and introduce a StatsResponse { name, downloads } Serialize DTO for get_stats, colocated with the other DTOs.

fix_examples.after:
let response = PublishResponse { name, version: version.to_string(), deps };
Ok((axum::http::StatusCode::CREATED, Json(response)))

findings.fix_guide: 1. Reuse PublishResponse in multipart_publish (same shape, non-breaking). 2. Add StatsResponse struct with Serialize; use in get_stats. 3. Update tests/registry_tests.rs assertions if they match on raw json!. 4. cargo test -p buff-registry.

effort_estimate.breakdown: PublishResponse reuse 10m, StatsResponse DTO 10m, test updates 10m

detection_method.query: grep serde_json::json! in handlers.rs -> 4 hits; compare field sets against storage.rs DTOs

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path crates\buff-registry\src\handlers.rs -Pattern 'serde_json::json!'; Select-String -Path crates\buff-registry\src\storage.rs -Pattern 'pub struct PublishResponse'

confidence.rationale: Both code sites read in full; field sets compared name-by-name against the DTO definitions.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Wire shapes currently identical for the publish echo, so this is drift-risk not present-day breakage; framed as consistency finding per scope item (1).

findings.title: Registry mixes singular /api/v1/package and plural /api/v1/packages resource nouns
findings.description: Within the consistently-versioned /api/v1/ prefix (verified across all 9 package routes, L279-290), the v1.6 read endpoint is singular (/api/v1/package/{name}, L280) while all T57 additions are plural (/api/v1/packages/{name}/badges L283, /stats L284, POST /api/v1/packages/{name} L289, /{version}/download L290-295). /health, /ready and /auth/* are intentionally unprefixed (probes/OAuth). The noun split is a REST-consistency wart, documented as-is in crates/buff-registry/AGENTS.md.
findings.root_cause: T126 (v1.6) established singular /package; T57 later added the plural /packages family without aliasing or migrating the original route.
findings.impact: Low: discoverability friction and a permanent two-conventions surface for the same resource; any future deprecation of /package must respect the stability promise. No functional breakage today.
findings.recommendation: Do NOT rename /api/v1/package (breaking). Add a plural alias GET /api/v1/packages/{name} (same handler) and mark singular as legacy in docs; or record the split as accepted in a decision file.

fix_examples.after:
.route("/api/v1/package/{name}", get(handlers::get_package))
.route("/api/v1/packages/{name}", get(handlers::get_package)) // plural alias; POST arm unchanged

findings.fix_guide: 1. Add the GET alias arm in lib.rs::app(). 2. Add a oneshot test asserting the plural GET returns PackageMetadata. 3. Note the alias in the HTTP API table. 4. cargo test -p buff-registry.

confidence.rationale: Route table read in full; split is objective. Uncertainty only whether maintainers consider it intentional, hence info severity.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The inconsistency is real and line-cited, but already visible in the crate's own documented HTTP API table, so a reviewer may classify it as accepted design; severity set to info and recommendation avoids any breaking rename.
